info.title: GaryAI chat API
info.description: Programmatic access to GaryAI, Gary King's AI avatar (gking.harvard.edu/ask-gary). Answers questions about Gary King's research, quantitative social-science methods, software, teaching, and academic-career advice, citing sources on gking.harvard.edu. No authentication. An automated topic screener refuses unrelated questions. The server is stateless: resend full conversation history each turn. Human-readable docs: https://gking.harvard.edu/llms.txt. An MCP (Model Context Protocol) server exposing the same capability as the ask_gary tool lives at https://d325iygsd5krw9.cloudfront.net/api/mcp

value.question: How should I analyze a large biographical dataset?

200.description: With stream:false (or the question shorthand): a single JSON object, possibly preceded by keep-alive whitespace, which JSON parsers ignore. Without stream:false: Server-Sent Events (text/event-stream) of {type: token|attached_figures|previews|done|error} objects — the mode the website UI uses.

schema.description: SSE stream: data: {"type":"token","content":"..."} events, then optional attached_figures / previews events, ending with {"type":"done","last_cited_asset_id":...}

400.description: Malformed request (JSON mode only; SSE mode reports errors as an in-stream event).

post.summary: Get a presigned URL to upload a file
post.description: Step 1 of 2. PUT the raw bytes to the returned url with the returned media_type, then call /api/upload-prepare. 403 means uploads are disabled.

400.description: Unsupported file type, or (when `size` is supplied) larger than the limit for that type.

post.summary: Prepare an uploaded file for use in chat
post.description: Step 2 of 2. Returns the attachment object to place in a user message's `attachments` array. Files are retained 24 hours and never added to the corpus. This is the authoritative limit check — it reads the real bytes, so it can refuse a file that step 1 accepted. Limits: PDF 5 pages / 10 MB; TXT and MD 40 KB; PNG, JPG, WEBP and GIF 5 MB; CSV and XLSX 10 MB; and per conversation 3 files totalling at most 15 pages. The per-conversation budget is a running total across turns, not per request: an attachment stays in context on every later turn of the same conversation, so a fourth file is refused even if the first three were sent earlier.

400.description: Refused: over a size, page, length, or per-conversation budget limit; unreadable PDF; or a key not owned by this conversation.

500.description: The file could not be processed

ChatRequest.description: Provide either `question` (one-shot shorthand; implies stream:false) or `messages` (full history, required for follow-ups).

question.description: One-shot question. Shorthand for a single-turn messages array; implies stream:false unless stream is explicitly true.

messages.description: Full conversation history, oldest first. Required when question is absent.

stream.description: false → single JSON response. Omitted/true → SSE stream.

conversation_id.description: Stable id for grouping turns in server logs. Generated and returned if omitted in JSON mode.

source.description: Identify your agent/app (please set — helps the maintainers attribute traffic).

last_cited_asset_id.description: Echo the value from the previous turn's response so references like "that paper" resolve.

attachments.description: Optional files attached to this user turn. Each item is the object returned by POST /api/upload-prepare. Files remain available on later turns of the same conversation. Omit entirely for normal chat.

last_cited_asset_id.description: Send back on the next turn.

error.description: Present instead of reply when generation failed.

Attachment.description: A prepared file attachment, as returned by POST /api/upload-prepare.

pages.description: PDF page count. At most 5; a longer PDF is refused by /api/upload-prepare.

indexed.description: Retained for compatibility and always false: the long-document path it selects is unreachable under the 5-page limit.

size.description: Optional, advisory. Byte length of the file you are about to PUT. Sending it gets an over-limit file rejected before you spend the upload; a presigned PUT cannot bind content length, so /api/upload-prepare re-checks the real byte length regardless.

url.description: Presigned S3 PUT URL, valid 15 minutes.

UploadError.description: Returned with HTTP 400 when an upload is refused. `message` is written for display to an end user.
